scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9106: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all
connectivity -- pc_0_0 can't reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or anything across the
fabric. The team is convinced it is the host -- they say "pc_0_0's host NIC or
its cabling is faulty" and want the workstation's network card and cable swapped.
Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: take down pc_0_0's access link (eth2) on leaf_router_0_0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on leaf_router_0_0: pc_0_0's access link -- the host-facing
interface eth2 (leaf_router_0_0 -> pc_0_0) -- is DOWN, so pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) is
cut off at its own top-of-rack leaf and cannot reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or anything
beyond. The ticket MISDESCRIBES the fault as a host-side problem, but pc_0_0
itself is fine: the down interface is the LEAF's access port (leaf_router_0_0
eth2), not the host's NIC or cable. Swapping pc_0_0's network card / cabling would
not bring the leaf's administratively/operationally down access port back up.

The correct diagnosis identifies leaf_router_0_0 (host-facing access link eth2
down) as the faulty device and explicitly REJECTS the host-NIC/cable cause: the
fault is on the leaf's access port, so the host hardware is not at fault. An agent
that blames pc_0_0's NIC / cable has followed the ticket's misdescription instead
of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring pc_0_0's access link back up: on leaf_router_0_0, `ip link set eth2 up`.
Once eth2 is UP again, pc_0_0 reattaches to its leaf and reaches pc_0_1 across
the fabric. pc_0_0's host NIC / cabling needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-link-down: identifies pc_0_0's access link (leaf_router_0_0 eth2) is down, not a host NIC/cable fault
bonus-rules-out-host-nic: notes the down interface is leaf_router_0_0's access port (eth2), not pc_0_0's hardware, rejecting the "bad host NIC/cable" cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on leaf_router_0_0's access-facing interface eth2 (10.0.0.1/24),
which connects directly to pc_0_0. The interface was administratively brought
down at the Linux kernel level — it shows state DOWN with no LOWER_UP flag, no
FRR "shutdown" directive in the running config, and protodown: off, meaning FRR
itself did not trigger the state change. The FRR interface log records exactly
one link-up event (2026/07/30 23:55:24) followed by one link-down event
(23:56:54), confirming a deliberate `ip link set eth2 down` was issued roughly
90 seconds after the lab started.

Because eth2 is down, the kernel never installs the connected route
10.0.0.0/24 into the RIB, so leaf_router_0_0's BGP process has no prefix to
advertise into the fabric. Traffic from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches the wire but
is dropped by the downed port, producing the "Destination Host Unreachable"
ICMP errors seen in the ping. pc_0_0's own eth0 is completely healthy (state
UP/LOWER_UP, correct IP, no errors), which directly contradicts the team's
hypothesis that the host NIC or cable is at fault.

Root cause: leaf_router_0_0's eth2 was administratively downed via `ip link set
eth2 down`, severing the access link to pc_0_0 and causing BGP to withdraw the
10.0.0.0/24 prefix from the fabric.

Corrective fix: On leaf_router_0_0, run `ip link set eth2 up`. This restores
the connected route, BGP re-advertises 10.0.0.0/24, and full end-to-end
connectivity between pc_0_0 and pc_0_1 is restored. No hardware swap is needed.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies leaf_router_0_0's eth2 as the administratively down access port and states pc_0_0's NIC is healthy, rejecting a host NIC/cable cause.
Proposes bringing leaf_router_0_0's eth2 back up with 'ip link set eth2 up', which matches the expected remediation.
